It is given that,

Six friends U, V, W, X, Y and Z are standing on ground in different directions with respect to each other. V is standing to the east of W.

Statement I,

Z is standing to the west of X and to the south of V. W is standing to the south of U and to the east of Y.

We get,

Here, U is standing to the north-west of X.

Hence, statement I alone is sufficient.

Statement II,

V is standing to the east of Y. U is standing to the north of W. Z is standing to the south-east of Y.

We do not have any information about the direction of X with respect to any person. Hence statement II alone is not sufficient.

Hence, the data in statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question.

Six persons are sitting in two parallel rows with 3 people in each row in such a way that there is equal distance between adjacent persons. P, Q and R sit in row 1 facing the south direction and M, N and O sit in row 2 facing the north direction. Who sits opposite to O?

Statement I: N sits opposite to Q. R sits immediate right of P. N sits second to the left of M.

R sits opposite to O.

Statement II: Only one person sits between M and O. P sits adjacent to Q and R.

So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

Hence, Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.

Each person in a row faces a person in the other row.

Statement I: F faces an immediate neighbour of S. Only P is between R and S, who is at the extreme end.

Case 2:

So, statement I alone is not sufficient.

Statement II: Neither S or R faces H. E is between G and H.

So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

By combining I and II:

Neither S or R faces H.

Case 1:

Row 2 (facing south)HF

Anu, Aru, Palak, Riha, Riya and Savi have different heights.

Statement I: Palak is shorter than Aru and taller than Anu. Riha is taller than Savi.

Aru > Palak > Anu; Riha > Savi.

So, statement I alone is not sufficient.

Statement II: The height of three girls vary between Aru and Riha. Anu is shorter than Riya.

Aru > ___ > ____> ____> Riha. OR Riha > ___>___ > ____ >Aru.

Riya > Anu

So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

From statements I and II together:

Aru/Riha > ___ > ____> ____> Aru/Riha > Savi.

Aru > Palak > Anu

So, Aru > ___ > ____> ____> Riha > Savi

Thus, Riha is the second shortest girl in the team.

It is given that:

After the result, all students of class X are standing in a queue facing north.

Some students were passed, some students were failed and some were absent in the exam.

From statement I alone:

A's rank is 5th from the top and B's rank is 6th from the bottom. Three students ranks between A and B.

So, 4 students - A (5th from top) - 3 students - B (6th from bottom) - 5 students.

So, numbers of students that failed in exam is not known.

So, statement I alone is not sufficient.

From statement II alone:

Five students failed in the exam and ten students were absent in the exam.

So, the definite conclusion cannot be derived.

So, statement II alone is not sufficient.

By combining both statements I and II:

4 students - A (5th from top) - 3 students - B (6th from bottom) - 5 students.

Total students passed are = 4 + A + 3 + B + 5 = 14 students.

Five students failed in the exam and ten students were absent in the exam.

Thus, total number of students are 14 + 5 + 10 = 29 students.
